Section 1

What this is

GPT and Claude already read 0.3.1 from the reference. You closed what they found. This is the same job against 0.3.2: an interpreter derived from the text, a new corpus, and the places two honest implementations can still diverge.

The headline is not “the compiler is wrong.” It is that a local can be in scope without ever having been assigned; that main’s parameter names are required and conventional at once; and that string identity, return unwinding, and argv layout are still silent.

Section 2

Contradiction

Contradiction · §1 vs §9

main parameter names

Section 1: “Conventionally they are named argc and argv.” Section 9: “main must accept exactly (argc argv).”

“Conventionally” means the names are a convention. The diagnostic means they are the contract. This reading enforces the names, because a diagnostic table a third implementation is asked to match is the stronger sentence.

(fn main (a b)
  (return 0))

Ask. Delete “conventionally”, or drop the name check and keep arity-2. Add tests/negative/main_wrong_names.llr once you pick.

Section 3

Gaps

Gap · headline · §3

Uninitialized locals after a let that never ran

A let is a static declaration plus a dynamic assignment. Source-order scope means x is visible after an untaken branch. The reference never says what x contains.

(fn main (argc argv)
  (if 0 (block (let x 1)))
  (return x))

A zero-filling interpreter, a poison interpreter, and a native 2,048-byte frame of stack garbage are all licensed. This oracle zero-fills. Probe exits 0.

Ask. Specify that every local slot is 0 until its let executes — the only option that keeps native and oracle comparable.

Gap · §3

Is a let initializer in scope of the name?

(let x x)

“From the point of its let” can mean the name token or the completed form. This reading allows it and yields 0. Recommend: the initializer is not in scope.

Gap · §2

String-literal identity

(== "a" "a")

Same address or not? Unspecified. This oracle does not intern (exits 0). A coalescing native image will return 1, and the 0.3.0 oracle gate can fail on a program the spec authorises both to accept.

Gap · §4

Empty form ()

The example of a non-identifier head is (1 2). () has no first element. This reading rejects it as expected form name.

Gap · §4 vs §5–7

Operand-count exactness is only claimed for §5–7

(let x 1 2), (while 1 (block) 0), (return 1 2) are not covered. This reading treats §4 forms as exact too. Move the sentence, or table the arities.

Gap · §4, §10

return unwinding

(return (+ (return 1) (/ 1 0)))

This reading exits 1 and does not trap. Write that return is a non-local exit of the current function that skips remaining operands.

Gap · §8

argv wording

“Points to argc NUL-terminated strings followed by a null pointer” is char* concatenated, or char**? This reading lays out a Linux pointer table. Ask: “argv is a pointer to argc pointers to NUL-terminated strings, followed by a null pointer.”

Gap · §2

SIGSEGV numeric status

The reference says SIGSEGV. It never says 139. Changelog fixtures use 139. Python subprocess reports −11. Treat death-by-signal as matching regardless of wait encoding.

Gap · §3–5

Three namespaces, never named

(fn + (a b) (return 99))
(fn main (argc argv)
  (return (+ (call + 1 2) 1)))   ; 100

Locals, functions, and builtin forms are different lookups. No reserved-word list. One paragraph under §3.

Section 4

Suggested 0.3.3

  1. Resolve §1 vs §9 on main names.
  2. Specify local-slot initial value (recommend 0).
  3. Initializer of let is not in scope of the name.
  4. String-literal identity is not to be depended on.
  5. return is a non-local function exit.
  6. argv is char**.
  7. Exact operand counts cover §4; name ().
  8. Name the three namespaces.

None of these require a code-generation change if the native compiler already zero-fills, does not intern, and already rejects (fn main (a b) …). If it does not zero-fill, (2) is a real native/oracle split and should be gated.
